text:
Marta: quick heads-up. After the recent SDK opt-in that flipped routing metadata to x-routing-policy-v2, our quota dashboard is showing a ~22% attribution shortfall for some tenants. Spotted during a routine ledger check.
Owen: which SDKs toggled it? TS/Go?
Marta: TS + Go canary groups flipped the runtime flag yesterday. Python is still on the old header for now.
Sasha: ok this is new header territory. console parsing only looks for x-routing-hint and falls back to x-tenant-id. x-routing-policy-v2 isn't recognized so rows are labeled unattributed.
Hector: proxy canonicalizer intentionally strips unknown headers for safety. We didn't whitelist x-routing-policy-v2 because RFC labeled it experimental.
Priya: customers with custom routing (affinity/cost-tier) saw behavior differences too. affinity cache misses spiked for those tenants.
Marta: immediate mitigation idea: add a reversible proxy shim that copies x-routing-policy-v2 -> x-routing-hint when present, and add x-routing-sourced: v2 so we can distinguish mapped traffic. Low risk, fast rollback.
Owen: agree that's the fastest path. Also emit a metric routing.header.mapped{from:v2,to:hint} so we can track how much traffic is affected.
Sasha: console changes will take longer to roll -- parsing, schema, and telemetry dashboards. Proxy mapping + telemetry event buys us runway.
Hector: I'll open CR-7724. Proposed rollout: canary to infra-zone-3 in 20m, monitor 45m, then ramp 3h. infra-bot: change created CR-7724, awaiting owner.
Marta: owner = Hector. Add test cases for affinity cache (simulate tenant with sticky hash) and billing reconciliation.
Owen: SDK action: dual-write both headers for a compatibility window (recommend 60 days). When opt-in=true, SDK should send x-routing-policy-v2 AND x-routing-hint (legacy). Add header x-routing-compat: dual to detect dual-writes.
Priya: good. For analytics we need to be careful: mapping could conflate deliberate v2 routing semantics with legacy semantics. So console should surface a small indicator if x-routing-sourced: v2 was mapped and let product/ops review before we auto-change policies.
Sasha: For telemetry, plan to: 1) increment routed.header.mapped metric; 2) tag logs with routing.mapping_source; 3) create a dashboard panel showing mapped vs native attribution by tenant.
Hector: proxy mapping implementation (canary snippet):
```
# proxy config: copy v2 header to legacy hint and tag as mapped
PATCH /infra/v1/proxy/configs/route_copy
{ "copy_from": "x-routing-policy-v2", "copy_to": "x-routing-hint", "tag_header": "x-routing-sourced", "tag_value": "sdk-v2" }
```
Owen: quick risk callouts: 1) mapping must NOT alter the routing payload (we must preserve the hash/fingerprint bytes). 2) don't change TTLs used by affinity cache. 3) ensure downstream services see the mapped header in the same request context.
Marta: test checklist for canary: a) quota unattributed rate < baseline + 1% after mapping b) affinity miss-rate unchanged c) no increase in 5xxs or p95 latency d) ledger totals reconcile within 0.1% after 24h.
Priya: I'll draft the customer note: "If you enabled routing-policy-v2 on SDKs, we've temporarily mapped it to our routing header so your quota attribution continues uninterrupted. Please upgrade to SDK >= upcoming-minor which will dual-write headers; we'll publish a deprecation timeline for legacy header emission."
Sasha: console PR to accept x-routing-policy-v2 is queued but lower priority than the shim. We'll also add a column in the quota dashboard showing "mapped?" so support can filter.
Owen: release steps: 1) proxy shim canary (Hector) 2) telemetry increment + dashboard (Sasha) 3) SDK dual-write release (Owen + SDK leads) 4) console parser change (Sasha) 5) deprecation schedule and customer comms (Marta)
infra-bot: scheduled canary window 20m-2h UTC for CR-7724.
canary-bot: Proxy config v2026.4 canary queued for infra-zone-3.
Hector: rolling the canary now. Will monitor routing.header.mapped and the unattributed metric and report back in 30m.
Marta: thanks all. Logging this thread as the single source for the incident and follow-ups. :thumbsup:
